transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I... I guess I'm here because things have just gotten really dark lately. I've been working at the vet clinic for almost twenty years now, and we've been so understaffed. Actually, just last week we had this golden retriever come in—sweetest thing you've ever seen, named Buster—and he had swallowed a whole tennis ball. Can you believe that? The owner was frantic, and I had to prep him for emergency surgery while juggling three other cases. It's just non-stop, you know? 

But anyway, what actually scared me enough to finally make an appointment is... well, I keep thinking it would just be so much easier if I didn't wake up at all. It's like this heavy blanket over me. And sometimes, when I'm driving home from the clinic after a long shift—especially on that stretch of highway past the old mall, they really need to fix the potholes there, it's terrible for your suspension—I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just... didn't turn the wheel.
Have you had thoughts of not waking up or harming yourself at any other times besides when driving?

Well, I... I don't really know. I guess it's mostly in the car, or maybe when I'm just lying in bed staring at the ceiling. My bedroom ceiling has this water stain, actually. It's shaped exactly like a map of Australia. I've been meaning to call the landlord about it for months, but he's just so difficult to deal with. He always complains about the cost of everything, like when the water heater broke last winter and we were without hot water for three days. Three days! Try washing scrub suits in freezing cold water, it's impossible to get the smell of anal glands out. 

But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, right. The thoughts. Yeah, I don't know, they just kind of pop up sometimes. It's hard to keep track.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

No, not really. That's actually another thing that's been bothering me. I usually love photography and gardening. I've got this beautiful little patch of heirloom tomatoes out back—well, usually I do. This year I haven't even bothered planting the seeds. The soil just sat there. And the squirrels keep getting into the bird feeders, which usually I'd go out and fix, or at least watch them, but lately I haven't checked them with any real interest at all. 

Actually, the squirrels around my neighborhood are getting so brazen. One of them chewed right through the plastic lid of my neighbor's trash can last week. Mrs. Higgins was furious, she came over complaining about it for twenty minutes while I was trying to leave for work. She's always complaining about something, though. If it's not the squirrels, it's the mailman being late, or the noise from the garbage trucks. 

But anyway, yeah, I haven't even touched my camera in months, either. I used to go out to the state park every Sunday morning to take macro shots of insects and dew on the leaves. I had this great macro lens I saved up for... but now it's just sitting in its case collecting dust. It's really frightening, honestly, because doing all those things—the garden, the birds, the photography—that used to be how I felt like myself, you know? And now it's just... nothing.
Do you often feel guilty about things?

I do. All the time, lately. It's just... things are so chaotic at home, and I keep telling myself I'm a terrible person for resenting the disruption. My husband's sister has been staying with us, actually. She's going through this awful divorce—her husband apparently ran off with his physical therapist, if you can believe the cliché. And she just leaves her things everywhere. Yesterday I tripped over her yoga mat in the hallway and spilled my coffee all over the rug. It's that nice Persian rug we got at an estate sale years ago, the one with the deep reds and blues. I spent an hour trying to scrub the stain out with club soda, but I think it's ruined. 

But, anyway, I just... I get so impatient. I replay every impatient look I give them, or every sharp comment I make, and I just use it as proof that my husband and the family would be better off without me. I'm just making everything worse for everyone. I mean, my sister-in-law is already crying half the day on our sofa—which, by the way, is a microfiber sofa, and it shows every single water spot, so her tears are literally leaving marks on the cushions. I tried telling her to use a tissue, but then I felt so guilty for caring about the furniture when her marriage is falling apart. I just... I feel like I'm failing at being a decent human being.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight lately?

Well, my appetite has been completely all over the place. I haven't really been weighing myself, but my clothes fit differently. Lately, I mostly just pick at a piece of toast in the morning or have some coffee. Oh, speaking of coffee, we just got this new espresso machine at the clinic. Dr. Evans bought it because he said morale was low, which, frankly, it is. The receptionist, Brenda, quit last week without any notice, just left her key on the desk and walked out, so we've been double-booking appointments and dealing with angry clients. One guy yelled at me for ten minutes because his golden retriever's nail trim was running late. People can be so entitled, you know? Like, we're doing the best we can, but we only have two hands. 

But yeah, the food thing... I just get to the end of a long clinic shift, like after dealing with Brenda's mess and the angry clients and everything, and I realize I've barely eaten a single thing all day. I just don't have the desire to.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and agitated?

I haven't really noticed anything like that. No, I don't think I'm moving any slower, and I'm not really restless either. It's just... I don't know, it's just the tiredness, I guess. Though, actually, speaking of moving, I did have to move a whole pallet of dog food at work the other day because the delivery guy just left it right in the middle of the receiving area. It was that premium brand, you know, the one with the salmon and sweet potato that costs a fortune? Anyway, he just dumped it there, and I had to haul it all into the storage room myself. My back was aching for two days after that. I really need to get a new mattress, too. My husband wants a memory foam one, but I heard they trap heat, and with my hot flashes lately, that sounds like a nightmare. But yeah, no, I haven't noticed any weird slowing down or anything.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

I... no. No, not really. I used to love photography, you know? I'd take my camera out into the backyard every weekend. I haven't touched it in months. I haven't even checked the bird feeders with any real interest, or cared what's coming up in the garden. Which is honestly frightening because those things used to be how I felt like myself. I had this whole setup for the hummingbirds, this beautiful glass feeder I found at a craft fair in Vermont. We went there for our anniversary three years ago. Or was it four? No, three, because it was right before we had to replace the transmission in the Subaru. That car was such a money pit. We finally traded it in for a Honda, which is so much more reliable, but the seats aren't nearly as comfortable for long trips. We drove it down to Florida last winter to see my parents, and my sciatica was acting up the whole way down I-95. The traffic around Washington D.C. was just unbelievable. We sat on the bridge for an hour and a half just staring at the Potomac. But yeah, the garden, the birds... I just look out the window now and I feel absolutely nothing. It's just another chore I can't bring myself to do.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, it's been... I'd say this whole thing has been hanging over me for about 11 months now. Yeah, 11 months. It just sort of settled in, you know? Though this past month has just been completely unbearable. Everything feels so heavy. It's funny, actually, thinking about 11 months ago, because that was right around the time my sister adopted this rescue greyhound, Barnaby. He's a sweet dog, but he has the worst separation anxiety. She can't even go to the grocery store without him howling the house down. She bought one of those fancy pet cameras where you can toss treats to them from your phone, but he just ignores the treats and stares at the camera. It's kind of creepy, honestly. I told her she should try one of those thunder shirts, we recommend them all the time at the clinic, but she read some blog post that said they restrict their natural energy flow or something ridiculous like that. She's always reading those holistic pet blogs. Last year she tried feeding him a raw vegan diet, which is just absurd for a dog, and he ended up with terrible diarrhea on her new Persian rug. But yeah, anyway, the depression... it's been about 11 months of this dark cloud, and lately it's just gotten so much worse.
Have you felt like you're fidgeting or having trouble sitting still lately?

Actually, yes, there was a stretch recently where I was exactly like that. For several days, I just couldn't sit still after I got home from work. I was pacing all through the house, taking a tape measure to all the rooms... I think I was trying to see if we had space for one of those massive, floor-to-ceiling cat trees. We had this gorgeous Maine Coon come into the clinic that week—huge boy, weighed almost twenty pounds, and his owner is this lovely older gentleman who always brings us donuts from that bakery on 4th Street. Have you been there? Their apple fritters are just incredible, but you have to get there before 9 AM or they're completely sold out. My husband loves the blueberry cake ones, but I think they're way too sweet. 

Anyway, I was just buzzing around, making all these elaborate lists, and I ended up completely reorganizing the kitchen cabinets long after everyone else had gone to bed. I actually found a tin of smoked paprika in the back that expired in 2018. Can you believe that? People just hoard spices, but they really lose all their flavor after a year or two. I ended up throwing out half the pantry. But yeah, for those few days, I just could not stop moving around the house.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past 11 months?

I haven't really weighed myself, but my appetite has been completely all over the place. Lately, I just pick at a piece of toast in the morning, maybe have a cup of coffee, and then I'll get to the end of a long shift at the clinic and realize I've barely eaten a thing all day. It's just so busy there right now. We had three emergency surgeries yesterday alone. One was this poor golden retriever who swallowed a whole pair of pantyhose. You wouldn't believe the things dogs eat. Last month, we pulled a squeaker toy, a handful of gravel, and a Barbie shoe out of a French bulldog. The owner was so embarrassed, she kept apologizing and saying she watches him like a hawk, but you know how fast they are. They just vacuum up anything on the floor. It reminds me, I really need to get my vacuum repaired. It's a Dyson, and it's supposed to be top of the line, but it keeps making this awful high-pitched squealing noise whenever I try to use it on the area rug in the living room. My husband says it's probably just a belt, but he said that about the washing machine two years ago and we ended up having to buy a whole new one. We got a front-loader this time, which uses so much less water, but you have to leave the door open or it gets that terrible mildew smell. But anyway, yeah, I'm just not eating much. I don't even have an appetite for dinner when I get home.
Have you been feeling restless or agitated most of the time over the past few weeks?

No, not really... I mean, I'm just so exhausted lately. I don't have the energy to be restless or agitated. It's more like I just want to sink into the couch and never get up. I did buy a new couch recently, actually. Well, not recently, maybe six months ago. It's this deep navy blue velvet, which I thought would look so elegant, but let me tell you, velvet is a nightmare with pet hair. Even though I don't have pets of my own right now, I bring home so much fur on my scrubs from the clinic. I have to use those sticky lint rollers constantly. I buy them in bulk from Costco now. Have you seen the size of the packages they sell there? It's ridiculous, but you really do save money in the long run. My husband went last weekend and came back with a tub of mayonnaise that could probably last us until the next decade. He always gets carried away in the snack aisle, too. But anyway, no, I haven't been feeling restless. Mostly just completely drained.
Have you been feeling like you're moving slower than usual lately?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. It feels like I'm moving through molasses most days. Just getting out of bed and getting dressed takes twice as long as it should. I used to be able to jump up, shower, and be out the door in twenty minutes flat. I had this whole routine down perfectly. I even timed my coffee maker to start exactly when my alarm went off. It's one of those programmable ones, a Cuisinart, I think. We got it as a wedding anniversary gift from my sister-in-law. She always gives the most practical gifts. Last year she gave us a set of those silicone baking mats, which I thought I'd never use, but they are actually amazing for roasting vegetables. You just toss some Brussels sprouts with olive oil and a little bacon grease... oh, bacon grease makes everything better, doesn't it? My grandmother used to keep a coffee can of it right on the stove. You probably can't do that anymore, health inspectors would have a fit. At the clinic, we have to be so careful about cross-contamination and keeping everything sterile. But anyway, yeah, I just feel so heavy and slow lately, like every little movement is a huge effort.
Have you been feeling like you're fidgeting or having trouble sitting still lately?

No, not really. Like I said, I'm just too exhausted to be fidgety. I don't think I've had the energy to tap a foot in months. I just sit there. Sometimes I'll just sit in my car in the driveway for twenty minutes after work before I can muster the strength to go inside. The car is so quiet, you know? It's a Subaru Outback, and the soundproofing is surprisingly good. We bought it specifically because it has all that cargo space in the back. We thought we'd go camping a lot, load up the tent and the cooler and head up to the mountains on the weekends. My husband bought this massive Yeti cooler that weighs a ton even when it's empty. He insisted it was an investment because it keeps ice frozen for a week, but honestly, when are we ever going to need ice for a whole week? We usually only go for two nights anyway. And the last time we went, it rained the entire time. The tent leaked right over my side of the air mattress, so I woke up in a puddle of freezing water. I was miserable. We ended up packing up in the dark and driving to a diner for breakfast at four in the morning. They had the most amazing blueberry pancakes, though. The syrup was actually real maple, not that high-fructose corn syrup stuff they usually give you. But yeah, no fidgeting. Just feeling like lead.
Have you been feeling an internal restlessness that makes you want to move around or engage in activities?

Well, not right now... right now I just want to sleep. But, oh gosh, maybe a couple of months ago? I was so wired. I couldn't stop. I ended up picking up all these extra shifts at the clinic, which is crazy because we were already short-staffed and everyone was stressed. But I just felt like I could handle it all. And then I came home and decided I needed to completely redo our whole household care schedule. I was contacting contractors to fix the deck, trying to coordinate my husband's chores, my chores, the yard work... I was treating it like I was managing a major hospital project or something. Nobody even asked me to do it. I just had to. Oh, and speaking of contractors, do you know how hard it is to get someone to just come out and give an estimate these days? I called five different places just to look at the wood rot on the back steps. One guy finally showed up, drove a truck that looked like it had been through a war zone, and quoted me a price that could have paid for a new car. I mean, lumber is expensive, I get it. My brother-in-law works at Home Depot, and he says the price of plywood fluctuates more than the stock market. He actually bought some stocks recently, some app on his phone where you can buy fractional shares. I don't really understand how that works. It seems like gambling to me. But yeah, I was just doing so much back then, like I was running on a motor that wouldn't shut off. Now, though... I'm just empty.
Have you been feeling an overwhelming need to engage in physical activity or talk excessively over the past few weeks?

Well, not in the past few weeks. Lately I've just been so drained. But, like I was saying about a couple of months ago, there was this period where I just couldn't stop moving. For several days, I'd get home from the clinic—and you know how exhausting it is wrestling big dogs onto the exam tables all day—but I'd get home and I just couldn't sit still. I was pacing through the whole house. I started measuring all the rooms for some reason. I think I had this idea that we needed to rip out all the carpets and put down hardwood. Hardwood is so much better when you have pets, anyway. We have a Golden Retriever mix, Bailey, and she sheds like you wouldn't believe. I swear I could knit a whole new dog from the fur I vacuum up every week. We use one of those Dyson animal vacuums. It's purple. My husband hates the color, but I told him, who cares what color it is if it actually picks up the hair? He's so picky about things like that. He wouldn't buy a perfectly good lawnmower once just because it was lime green. Can you imagine? But anyway, yeah, I was pacing, measuring everything, making all these lists of projects, and I was up reorganizing the kitchen cabinets long after everyone else was asleep. I just had to keep doing things.
Have you been feeling an internal pressure to keep moving or doing things over the past few weeks?

No, definitely not recently. Like I said, lately it's just been the opposite. I'm just so heavy and tired all the time. But it's funny you ask about pressure, because the water pressure in our shower has been absolutely terrible the last few weeks. I don't know if it's the pipes or the showerhead. My husband tried taking it off and soaking it in vinegar—he read online that vinegar dissolves calcium buildup. He's always looking up these DIY fixes on YouTube. Some guy with a thick Boston accent has a whole channel dedicated to plumbing repairs. It's actually kind of fascinating, the way they solder copper pipes together. But the vinegar didn't work at all, so now we're stuck with this pathetic little trickle of water. It takes me twice as long to rinse the shampoo out of my hair. I use this special oatmeal shampoo because my scalp gets so dry in the winter. We actually use an oatmeal shampoo on the dogs at the clinic, too, when they have allergies. It smells like cookies. But yeah, no internal pressure to move around lately, just feeling completely wiped out.
Have you been feeling like you're fidgeting or having trouble sitting still recently?

No, not recently at all. Honestly, I barely move from the couch these days. I just kind of sit there staring at the TV, not even really watching it. The other day, I think I sat through three whole episodes of some baking competition show before I even realized what was on. Have you seen those shows where they make cakes that look like real objects? Like, someone will cut into a shoe or a potted plant, and it's actually red velvet cake. It's wild. I don't know how they get the fondant to look like leather or dirt. I tried working with fondant once for my niece's birthday—she wanted a unicorn cake—and it was a total disaster. It kept tearing, and it tasted like sugary play-dough. I ended up just using buttercream and sticking a plastic horn on top. She didn't care, she was just happy it was pink. But yeah, no fidgeting lately. Just... sitting. Just feeling like lead.
Are there any activities that you still find yourself looking forward to or enjoying?

No, not really. That's the scariest part, honestly. I haven't even touched my camera in weeks. I used to love going out early to photograph the birds, but now I don't even check the feeders with any real interest. We have these squirrel-proof feeders, the ones with the little weight-activated cages that drop down? They're supposed to keep the gray squirrels out, but I swear the squirrels in our neighborhood are little acrobats. I watched one actually hang upside down from the shepherd's hook and just scoop the black oil sunflower seeds out with one paw. They're so smart. My husband wanted to grease the pole, but I read that's bad for the birds if they get it on their feathers. It messes up their waterproofing. You know, duck feathers are amazing like that, the way the water just beads right off them. We had a duck come into the clinic once that had gotten into some motor oil, and we had to wash it with Dawn dish soap, just like in those commercials. It took hours. But anyway, I don't even care what's coming up in the garden right now either. I usually have all my spring bulbs planned out, but... I don't know. It's frightening because taking pictures, the garden, the birds... those things used to be how I felt like myself. Now it's just nothing.
Have you had any periods over the past 11 months where you regained interest in your old hobbies, even if only for a short time?

No, not really. It's just been this... this heavy cloud hanging over me for about 11 months now. Even before this last month, which has just been completely unbearable, it was still there. Just a constant weight. It's funny you mention time, though, because 11 months ago was right around the time my sister adopted her greyhound. He's a retired racer, you know? They have these huge, barrel chests and these tiny little waists. They have to wear special coats in the winter because they don't have any body fat. She bought him this fleece one that makes him look like a little bumblebee. It's hilarious. But they have terrible teeth, greyhounds do. We see it at the clinic all the time. The soft food they feed them at the tracks just rots their teeth right out. We had to pull like eight teeth on this one poor guy last year. Dental cleanings on dogs are so stressful, though, because you have to put them under anesthesia. And sighthounds, like greyhounds, process anesthesia differently than other dogs, so you have to be really, really careful with the dosage. My sister was so nervous when he had his first cleaning. But yeah, no, I haven't really felt interested in anything for almost a year now. Just... nothing.
Have you experienced any periods of elevated mood or excessive energy over the past 11 months?

Well, yeah, actually. Earlier this month... it was weird. I felt almost electrically upbeat, just buzzing, you know? But then I was also snapping at everyone over the tiniest things. Like, someone misplaced a medication cup at the clinic, and I just lost it. Or they changed the morning schedule, and I got so angry. It didn't feel like me at all. Speaking of the clinic schedule, it's been an absolute nightmare lately because our receptionist went on maternity leave. She had a little boy, seven pounds, two ounces. She named him Liam, which is so popular right now. I feel like every other baby is named Liam or Noah. But anyway, without her, the phones just ring and ring. And people get so mad when they have to wait on hold. This one guy yelled at me because we couldn't get his cat in for a nail trim that same day. A nail trim! Like it's an emergency. Cats are so funny about their paws, though. Most of them hate having their toes touched. We have to do the "purrito" wrap with a towel just to keep them from scratching us to ribbons. Have you ever tried to pill a cat? It's impossible. They just spit it right back out, or they hide it in their cheek and wait until you're not looking. We use pill pockets, but half the time they just eat the treat and leave the pill on the floor. It's so frustrating. But yeah, that buzzing feeling and the snapping... it was just earlier this month. It was really strange.
